summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Solaris Health through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating tradeoffs between hosted API (fastest) vs Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and data isolation. Key concerns: SOC 2 controls, KMS integration, per-route cost attribution, and an initial pilot/benchmark. Agreed next steps: pricing + dedicated worksheet, run sample benchmarks, and provide security package.
topics: Cost breakdown and per-token unit economics
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood, I have Liam, our solutions engineer, with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Rao: Morning, doing well, thanks. Marcus and Elena are here too.
[00:12] Marcus Nguyen: Morning. Quick heads up, we only have 45 minutes so want to focus on the console analytics and the cost piece.
[00:20] Ava Martinez: Yep totally, that's the plan. We'll start with the usage analytics then dive into per-route dashboards and cost attribution. Liam will demo the console.
[00:28] Liam Chen: Cool, jumping in — share my screen — let me know if the slide or the live console comes through.
[00:36] [screen share noise]
[00:40] Liam Chen: Alright, top-left is overall token volume, you can filter by model, route, team, timeframe. For Solaris health folks, tagging routes by product (diagnostics, triage-chat, summarization) is easy and cost shows per route.
[00:52] Elena Torres: When you say cost per route, is that including batching and cache savings? We need to show business owners true unit economics.
[00:58] Liam Chen: Good question. The console shows raw per-token cost based on the chosen model and quantization profile, and then an 'adjusted cost' line that factors in automatic batching and prefix/KV cache hit rates. So you get both a raw and realistic cost.
[01:12] Dr. Priya Rao: That adjusted cost — is it simulated or based on observed logs? We need it to reflect what we'll actually pay.
[01:18] Liam Chen: It's based on observed request traces once enabled — we ingest token-level traces (anonymized) and compute effective tokens after batching and cache hits. There's also a simulator to project savings if you change batch sizes or enable cache TTL.
[01:30] [01:31] Marcus Nguyen: Can you break down how cache hits are measured? We're worried about KV cache correctness for conversation contexts.
[01:36] Liam Chen: We tag requests with a route-id and client session id, then compute prefix reuse. The KV cache metric is conservative — only counts exact prefix reuse, not semantic reuse. So it's a lower-bound estimate.
[01:47] Ava Martinez: Also important: you can set per-route budgets and alerts, and we expose per-API-key cost attribution so teams see chargebacks.
[01:56] Elena Torres: OK, that helps the finance team. On security, can we restrict who sees per-route PII?
[02:02] Liam Chen: RBAC at the console level — you can create roles, restrict dashboards, and we integrate with SSO / SAML. For data encryption, we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for the stored traces and audit logs.
[02:15] Dr. Priya Rao: Is audit logging exportable to our SIEM?
[02:19] Liam Chen: Yes, audit logs can be shipped via secure forwarder to your S3 or to a webhook. We also have API endpoints for event export.
[02:27] [02:28] Marcus Nguyen: On the cost side — show me an example breakdown for a triage-chat route.
[02:32] Liam Chen: Sure — switching to 'per-route' view — here we have triage-chat: 1.4M tokens last week, model is Aurora-13B quantized int8, effective batch size 16, cache hit 22%, raw cost $0.006/token => raw $8,400, adjusted $6,500 after batching/cache.
[02:51] Dr. Priya Rao: That adjusted number — does it include instance overhead for Dedicated?
[02:55] Liam Chen: Adjusted cost is compute + tokens. For Dedicated we allow you to amortize reserved capacity separately — the console has a 'Dedicated amortization' toggle that shows per-token amortized infra cost based on your committed GPUs and utilization.
[03:08] Elena Torres: If we go Dedicated for PHI workloads, what are the guarantees around isolation and backups?
[03:14] Ava Martinez: Dedicated offers tenant-isolated GPU pools, VPC peering options, and optional on-prem packaging. Backups and logs can be customer-managed in your S3 with KMS. We'll include the Dedicated SLA in the docs we send.
[03:26] [03:27] Marcus Nguyen: What about fallback — if a Dedicated node fails, do we overflow to hosted?
[03:31] Liam Chen: Yes, smart routing policies support fallback to hosted-compatible model variants — it's configurable per-route. You can set failover to lower-cost hosted or to another region.
[03:40] Dr. Priya Rao: Compliance — do you list specific certifications?
[03:43] Ava Martinez: We provide SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO27001 summary, and we can provide a security pack with our pen-test, architecture diagrams, and our KMS integrations. We'll attach that.
[03:55] Marcus Nguyen: Great. For the pilot, we want to test latency and cost on our busiest route and compare a hosted run vs Dedicated with quantization.
[04:03] Liam Chen: Sounds good. For latency — the per-route dashboard includes p50/p90/p99 latency buckets, broken down by model and region. You can filter to requests under a certain token range to get tail behaviour.
[04:15] [04:16] Dr. Priya Rao: Any chance to show the time-series view and an anomaly detection alert?
[04:20] Liam Chen: Yep — anomaly detection shows sudden increases in cost per token or spikes in latency. It's configurable and can tie to Slack or PagerDuty.
[04:28] Elena Torres: On RBAC and data access, can we limit the console view so only security sees raw request logs?
[04:33] Liam Chen: Yes — role definitions let you hide raw request payloads; people with 'auditor' role can see metadata and redacted transcripts; 'developer' role sees full traces.
[04:43] [04:44] Marcus Nguyen: Are there tagging best practices you recommend for per-route cost attribution?
[04:48] Ava Martinez: We usually recommend two tags: product_route and business_unit. Also include a team attribute and environment. That lets the console compute charts per tag and combine with cost center mapping.
[04:58] Dr. Priya Rao: Can tags be attached automatically from our API layer? We don't want to change a lot of code.
[05:03] Liam Chen: You can send route metadata as headers in the API call; we persist them at ingestion so little code change.
[05:09] [05:10] Marcus Nguyen: For the benchmarking we'll need a dataset and 1k concurrent sessions. Can you support that?
[05:15] Liam Chen: Yes, we can run an internal perf harness or you can provide a replay dataset. For Dedicated benchmarking we typically spin up equivalent capacity and run both hosted and dedicated runs to measure p99 latency and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:27] Dr. Priya Rao: Any limitations on model variants? We use a custom fine-tuned 13B occasionally.
[05:33] Liam Chen: We support custom model artifacts — for Dedicated we can bring custom weights; there are compatibility checks and we may need a short onboarding run to test kernels. For hosted we can also host customer models under Private deployments with VPC.
[05:45] Elena Torres: KMS — can we bring our AWS KMS keys for encrypting traces?
[05:49] Ava Martinez: Yes, customer-managed KMS supported. For Private deployments you'll hold keys in your account.
[05:55] [06:00] Marcus Nguyen: Pricing — can you go over the worksheet?
[06:03] Ava Martinez: Sure — the worksheet we'll send shows three components: per-token inference cost (by model & quantization), amortized infra cost for Dedicated (per-GPU monthly commit / utilization), and optional addons (observability retention, premium SLA). The console breaks cost by route and shows a forecast for the month based on historical volume.
[06:20] Liam Chen: I'll call out an example: in the triage-chat route, if you increase batch size from 8 to 16 you might see 10-18% token cost reduction but p99 could go up ~40ms depending on your latency SLO. Those tradeoffs are shown in the simulator.
[06:37] Dr. Priya Rao: Is there a way to run an A/B test for two model versions and show cost and quality delta?
[06:42] Liam Chen: Yes — rollouts support canary and A/B splits, with metrics for latency, cost, and custom quality signals. We can ingest eval prompts and compute difference in output scoring if you provide the eval harness.
[06:55] [07:00] Marcus Nguyen: For the pilot timeline — we want to start a 3-week pilot, run benchmarks week 1, week 2 test Dedicated with quantization, week 3 analyze quality and cost. Is that realistic?
[07:09] Ava Martinez: Yep that's a common cadence. We'll send a scope doc.
[07:13] Dr. Priya Rao: Any gotchas with healthcare data? PHI concerns?
[07:17] Elena Torres: (interject) We need to make sure logging is configured to redact PHI and that only encrypted traces leave our VPC.
[07:23] Liam Chen: For PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; we also support field-level redaction at ingestion and PII detection hooks.
[07:34] [07:35] Marcus Nguyen: Ok good. Can you also show the cost alerts and how they'd notify teams?
[07:39] Liam Chen: Alright switching back — config for alerts: threshold by daily spend, by route growth %, or by per-token cost increase. Notifications can be Slack, email, PagerDuty. You can scope alerts to teams.
[07:51] Dr. Priya Rao: We might want an alert when adjusted cost deviates from forecast by >10%.
[07:55] Ava Martinez: Noted, we'll include that in the pilot config.
[07:59] [08:00] Marcus Nguyen: Any mention of model compilation / kernel selection? That impacts throughput.
[08:04] Liam Chen: The runtime does model compilation and kernel selection automatically; for Dedicated we expose a tuning run where we pick best kernels and quantization profile for your model and seq-len distribution.
[08:16] Dr. Priya Rao: What's the overhead of quantization on quality? We need to measure hallucination risk.
[08:22] Liam Chen: Quantization can slightly change logits; we recommend A/B quality checks on key prompts. The console ties evals to rollouts so you can gate promotion on a quality threshold.
[08:34] [08:35] Elena Torres: Ok, last quick question — can we export per-route cost to our FinOps system?
[08:40] Liam Chen: Yes, export as CSV or via API. We also support direct ingestion into cost tools if you want a connector.
[08:48] Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks, this is helpful.
[08:50] Ava Martinez: Great — recap: we'll send pricing + dedicated worksheet, security pack (SOC 2 + KMS docs), and Liam will run a benchmark once Marcus uploads sample prompts.
[08:59] Marcus Nguyen: I'll upload the prompts by Tues. Thanks.
[09:02] Elena Torres: I'll review the security questionnaire and flag items.
[09:05] Ava Martinez: Perfect. We'll follow up with a pilot scope doc and proposed dates. Thanks everyone.
[09:09] [call ends]

Note: transcription contains occasional word swaps and timestamps are approximate. The demo included live console screens and links to: https://redwood.example/console/demo-dashboard (shared), pricing worksheet (sent after call), security-pack.zip (to be attached).
